reference: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon 1999, Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
footnote: One infraspecific inventory entry (Hymenopappus scabiosaeus var. corymbosus) is counted as an inventory entry, not as a separate biological species.

morphology.habit: Annual as part of the nonwoody broad Gutierrezia group; 0.1–0.8 m tall, much-branched above
morphology.leaves: Alternate, essentially sessile and linear, 0.6–2(–5) mm wide
morphology.heads: Campanulate radiate heads with 10–15 ray florets (species account), yellow rays and disks
morphology.reproductive: Disk florets fertile and producing cypselae; disk pappus of several short acute scales, ray pappus inconspicuous/absent (genus key); 7–13 disk florets in key
morphology.fruits: Cypselae puberulent with short purple hairs, fruit body visible (genus key)

issues: Original flora spells genus Guterrezia in one species paragraph but Gutierrezia in section heading: record spelling variation, not alternate taxon.
FNA recorded ray counts can differ among infraspecific concepts; avoid imposing one universal count.

morphology.habit: Taprooted annual 10–85 cm; stems not winged by decurrent leaves
morphology.leaves: Alternate, linear or threadlike mostly <2 mm wide; lowermost sometimes pinnatifid
morphology.heads: Usually globose yellow disks, about 10 yellow rays, ligules 5–10 mm
morphology.variety_key: var. amarum disk lobes yellow to yellow-brown, basal leaves often withered; var. badium disk lobes reddish brown/purplish, basal leaves often remaining and pinnatifid
morphology.habitat: Open woods, pastures, fields, disturbed areas
morphology.phenology: var. amarum May–Nov, var. badium Apr–Jul with occasional later flowering

issues: Do not infer leaf-base decurrence from mere ridged stems; original key explicitly says unwinged.

morphology.habit: Fibrous-rooted perennial from weakly rhizomatous base, stems 1(–2) m
morphology.leaves: Alternate, linear-elliptic; blades >2 mm wide and decurrent onto winged stems
morphology.heads: Yellow rays ~20, up to 15 mm long; yellow disks (genus key)

issues: Species-specific numeric involucre diameter not in 1999 treatment; do not import FNA dimensions without another source check.
Contrast annual winged H. elegans and unwinged H. amarum.

morphology.leaves: Alternate linear to narrow elliptic/lanceolate; decurrent stem wings; upper leaves much reduced, linear and entire
morphology.heads: Pedunculate above foliage; yellow rays sometimes red-brown blotched at base
morphology.discs: Disk-corolla lobes reddish or yellowish-brown according to genus key
morphology.habitat: Gravelly stream bottoms or limestone seep slopes

issues: Compare H. autumnale, perennial with both ray and disk corollas yellow; H. elegans is an annual.
Compare H. microcephalum with shorter rays 2–3(–5) mm and less-reduced upper leaves.

morphology.habit: Taprooted annual, height from about 10 cm to 4 m (variable wild and cultivated forms)
morphology.leaves: Lower leaves opposite, most alternate; triangular-ovate to ovate-lanceolate blades, truncate/cordate bases; large leaves 10–30 cm wide per key
morphology.phyllaries: Conspicuously ciliate, 4–7(–10) mm wide, tip abruptly contracted (key)
morphology.rays: Deep yellow, pistillate but infertile per genus treatment
morphology.discs: Brown-red, occasionally dark yellow; perfect and fertile
morphology.fruit: Disk-derived glabrous or pubescent cypselae; genus has readily shed pair of pappus awns

historical_names: Helianthus annuus subsp. lenticularis (Douglas ex Lindl.) Cockerell
issues: Contrast H. maximiliani perennial colonies with long folded narrow sessile leaves; avoid using head size alone.

morphology.leaves: Alternate, without distinct petiole; relatively broad 20–60(–90) mm in key, narrowly elliptic, often conspicuously lengthwise-folded and sickle-shaped
morphology.heads: Few to numerous in racemose/spike-like upper-stem array
morphology.rays: Yellow ligules about (15–)25–35(–40) mm, pistillate infertile (genus)
morphology.fruit: Disk-derived cypsela 3–4 mm; genus has readily detached two-awned pappus

issues: Flora describes leaf blade widths broader than some field summaries; preserve original printed-key figures without overriding other references.
Contrast sessile conduplicate blades against broad distinctly petiolate H. annuus.

morphology.habit: Woody-based perennial 15–60 cm, many stems in older plants
morphology.leaves: Alternate, crowded and entire; soft dense gray pubescence, non-glandular or nearly so; flowering-branch blades oblanceolate, roughly 3–5× as long as wide
morphology.heads: Yellow-rayed golden-aster heads; ligules 6–8 mm, yellow disk flowers
morphology.pappus: Genus ray pappus present, disk pappus long scabrous bristles plus short outer scales

issues: Contrast H. stenophylla resin-dotted green linear leaves with swollen-based stiff hairs.

morphology.leaves: Green, conspicuously resin-glandular, stiffly hairy with swollen hair bases; linear to narrow oblanceolate, about 8–15× as long as wide
morphology.heads: Yellow ray ligules ca. 10 mm with yellow disks (species/genus)
morphology.pappus: Genus ray pappus present; long scabrous bristles in disks
morphology.habitat: Sandy soils in western part of regional flora

issues: Leaf hair-base swellings require hand lens; plant color alone insufficient.

morphology.habit: Strongly camphor-scented glandular-pilose taprooted annual or biennial 20–200 cm
morphology.leaves: Alternate; mid/upper blades ovate, clasping or partly clasping; spring plants with coarse-toothed petiolate basal leaves, fall plants often much taller with upper auriculate-clasping foliage
morphology.fruit: Ray pappus absent per species branch of 1999 key

historical_names: Heterotheca subaxillaris var. latifolia (Buckley) Gandhi & R.D.Thomas
issues: Flora explicitly differentiates spring and summer/fall morphological forms; do not assume all leaf sizes correspond to distinct taxa.

morphology.leaves: Alternate, basal rosette plus stem leaves; basal blades coarsely once-pinnate to simple, segments 6–30 mm, often woolly below
morphology.phyllaries: Petaloid tips, 6–12 × 3–7 mm, white or red-tinged
morphology.discs: Corollas reddish-tinged, rarely entirely white, 3.5–5 mm
morphology.fruit: Obconical 4-angled pubescent cypsela; pappus 14–18 hyaline scales ≤1.5(–2) mm (genus)
morphology.habitat: Mainly sandy open woods and disturbed places

historical_names: Hymenopappus scabiosaeus var. artemisiifolius (DC.) Gandhi & R.D.Thomas
issues: Compare narrow ≤2–8 mm segments of H. scabiosaeus; habitat supplementary, not absolute.

morphology.leaves: Basal finely divided into slender linear/threadlike ultimate segments ≤1.5 mm wide; white woolly below possible
morphology.heads: Corymbose discoid clusters, no ray florets
morphology.phyllaries: Petaloid tips, 5–8 × 2–4 mm, last 1–2 mm yellowish
morphology.discs: White corollas 2–3 mm to lobe tip; corolla tube 1.5–2(–2.2) mm per key
morphology.habitat: Gravelly prairie, limestone outcrops, some sand

issues: A useful separation from H. artemisiifolius and H. scabiosaeus is segment width and short corolla length.

records.printed_flora_page: Hymenopappus scabiosaeus L'Hér. var. corymbosus (Torr. & A.Gray) B.L.Turner

morphology.habit: Biennial herb 0.4–1 m (variety description and genus)
morphology.leaves: Basal once-pinnate to bipinnate, ultimate segments 2–8 mm wide, finely divided; alternate cauline leaves
morphology.heads: Discoid heads in corymbose group, rays absent
morphology.phyllaries: 5–9 × 2–4 mm with white/yellowish petaloid 2–4 mm apical portions
morphology.fruit: Obconical four-angled pubescent cypselae with 14–18 hyaline pappus scales (genus)

issues: Explicit infraspecific treatment: don't copy to all H. scabiosaeus until accepted-rank concept reviewed.
Repository also lists H. scabiosaeus at species level; avoid duplicate-counting this variety as wholly separate biological species.

holds.reason: No 1999 species treatment here; needs FNA.

holds.name: Gymnosperma glutinosum
holds.reason: No 1999 species treatment here; needs FNA or Texas southwestern flora.

holds.name: Gaillardia amblyodon
holds.reason: Historical name and morphology unverified in 1999 volume, remains hold.
